newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungarian grains futures rise on weather,world mkt.
newsitem.headline: Hungarian grains futures rise on weather,world mkt.

text.p: Almost all Hungarian grains futures firmed on Friday due to the unseasonally hot and dry weather and a slight price rise on international markets, Budapest Commodity Exchange (BCE) traders said.
"If the weather does not change, the prices are likely to rise even further," said Robert Monostori of Agrimpex Kereskedelmi Kft.
Maize futures rose or remained steady as the weather made crop outlooks and the future movements of prices uncertain.
"Speculators do not dare to sell and neither do producers," Monostori said.
The bad weather enlivened feed barley futures, which usually change hands in low turnover or remain untraded. Feed barley firmed for all maturities.

Milling wheat and feed wheat futures rose for all maturities traded except August, which closed slightly lower as one market player wanted to sell for August even if it meant a lower price, traders said.

They said the price increases were also fuelled by the closing of short positions, opened by speculators and producers around February, when a falling trend on the world market sent Hungarian grains futures into a plunge.
